description: Canonical research questions and follow-on work. Statuses refer to the research, not completion of this website. No investigators or funding commitments are assigned.

items.title: Test collective purchasing benefits
items.question: Does pooled procurement improve price and service after dues, switching costs, and differences in privacy or quality?
items.nextStep: Obtain matched individual and collective offers, define comparable service conditions, and preregister net-benefit measures.
sourceTitles: Research program and falsifiable hypotheses
Business model and economic discipline

items.title: Test meaningful permission and refusal
items.question: Do members understand retrieval versus training permissions and successfully exercise refusal, withdrawal, and exit?
items.nextStep: Run compensated usability studies with low-risk fictional records and test actual revocation and export workflows.
sourceTitles: Research program and falsifiable hypotheses
Gmail, private AI, and meaningful opt-in

items.title: Measure supplier bargaining gains
items.question: Can collective representation improve contributors' net compensation and enforceable conditions without depending indefinitely on subsidy?
items.nextStep: Compare bounded licensing or stewardship offers, full transaction costs, repeat buyer demand, and contributor outcomes.
sourceTitles: Research program and falsifiable hypotheses
From digital Costco to a bargaining federation

items.title: Verify additional commons benefits
items.question: Do benefit covenants and funding awards improve maintenance and public access without enclosing open knowledge or merely replacing existing support?
items.nextStep: Choose matched open resources and measure additional maintenance, accessibility, steward autonomy, and continued lawful reuse.
sourceTitles: Research program and falsifiable hypotheses
Creative Commons as an aggregation model

items.title: Test representative club governance
items.question: Can buyer and supplier chambers plus an affected-party council prevent capture while keeping decisions practical and participation accessible?
items.nextStep: Rehearse admission, fees, conflicts, data-use changes, deadlock, and exit with compensated participants; record whose decisions change.
sourceTitles: From digital Costco to a bargaining federation
Research program and falsifiable hypotheses

items.title: Evaluate infrastructure bargaining
items.question: Can collective procurement and host-community representation measurably reduce externalized energy, water, and ratepayer burdens?
items.nextStep: Select a bounded site or procurement case, establish a credible comparison, and fund independent measurement and community review.
sourceTitles: Energy, data centers, and community bargaining
Research program and falsifiable hypotheses

items.title: Validate a bargaining agreement
items.question: Which representative mandates, contract terms, enforcement resources, and competition-law routes are defensible for the selected participants and jurisdiction?
items.nextStep: Compare existing instruments, commission local legal review, and test a redlined nonbinding framework before any executed pilot.
sourceTitles: Follow-on research: a Commons Bargaining Framework Agreement
Regulatory framework: present rules and proposals

items.title: Evaluate contextual reputation and ranking
items.question: Does eligibility-first, task-specific ranking predict successful outcomes while resisting manipulation and giving qualified newcomers fair exposure?
items.nextStep: Define a held-out evaluation, publish component metrics and uncertainty, and test conflicts, fake feedback, version changes, and appeals.
sourceTitles: Reputation, validation, and quality ranking

items.title: Assess commons-reinvestment credits
items.question: Can capped credits create additional public benefit at an acceptable administrative and fiscal cost without donor control, laundering, or double counting?
items.nextStep: Specify the tax base and counterfactual, model forgone treasury revenue, and independently review eligible spending and recipient protections.
sourceTitles: Data dividends, Pigouvian taxes, and commons credits

items.title: Test future AI demand
items.question: For a real application, does a governed contributor network outperform open data, direct licensing, or in-house collection on quality-adjusted total cost?
items.nextStep: Run a narrow paid pilot, compare held-out outcomes and full costs, and measure renewals, contributor burdens, coverage, and meaningful agency.
sourceTitles: Participation incentives and the future AI data club
A ninety-day starting sequence

items.title: Test what changes each infrastructure bargain
items.question: At each node, which combination of organized demand, credible alternatives, enforceable conditions, and independent evidence changes actual control or benefit allocation?
items.nextStep: Select a bounded node and counterparty, document the proposed lever, negotiate a measurable commitment, and test exit, audit, and remedies.
sourceTitles: New knowledge objects and technical architecture

items.title: Validate a minimum viable bargaining institution
items.question: Can a professionally operated Commons Bargaining Federation secure an enforceable agreement and demonstrable member benefits before taking on unnecessary institutional complexity?
items.nextStep: Choose a jurisdiction and founding cohort, fund counsel and enforcement, ratify a capped mandate, and compare credible vendor offers.
sourceTitles: Institution blueprint: a Commons Bargaining Federation
From digital Costco to a bargaining federation
